site.title: Longrun · RL environments for AI agents
site.description: Synthetic RL environments for personal agents and AI employees — realistic, dynamic, business-specific, and hard to game.

hero.title: Train AI agents inside the work they will actually do.
hero.subtitle: Synthetic RL environments for personal agents and AI employees — realistic, dynamic, business-specific, and hard to game.

sections.title: Digital workplaces for agents
sections.lead: Not another static benchmark. A repeatable world where an agent must actually finish the job.

cards.label: Personal agent
items: Re-plan a trip when a flight is cancelled
Coordinate email, calendar, bookings and documents
Resolve a return / subscription / service issue
Research options, compare constraints and prepare the action
cards.difficulty: The world changes while the agent is acting.

cards.label: AI employee
items: Resolve a customer escalation across CRM + support + billing
Prepare a renewal using account history, docs and internal chat
Triage an incident, coordinate owners and update the runbook
Execute finance / operations / legal workflows with policy constraints
cards.difficulty: Success means correct side effects, not a plausible answer.

sections.title: A production-grade RL environment

items.title: Realistic + complex
items.body: Long-horizon workflows across apps, people, files and permissions.

items.title: Non-stationary
items.body: Events happen while the agent acts; data, users and policies evolve.

items.title: Hard to hack
items.body: Hidden ground truth, randomized worlds, held-out seeds and verifier ensembles.

items.title: Built for business
items.body: Custom workflows, domain policy, private data shapes, auditability and controls.

sections.footnote: Design target: the model cannot win by memorizing patterns or exploiting one weak reward channel.

sections.title: Environment factory: from a business process to trainable worlds
sections.lead: Every environment ships as a self-contained, resettable unit with its own state, events, tasks and verifiers.

steps.title: World generator
steps.body: Org graph, accounts, files, histories, policies

steps.title: Tool layer
steps.body: CRM, email, docs, tickets, browser, DB, APIs

steps.title: Task + event engine
steps.body: Hidden goals, difficulty, interrupts, other actors

sections.defineNote: One world can generate many fresh episodes without manually labeling every trajectory.

sections.title: Environment Pack v1
sections.lead: 200 production-ready environments in 8 weeks. Start narrow, prove quality, then scale the factory.
sections.scaleTitle: Why 200 worlds can create much more than 200 examples
sections.scaleCaveat: Illustrative scale — actual episode count depends on task depth and QA gates.
sections.scaleNote: The scaling unit is the world generator, not the annotation workforce.

sections.title: A customer escalation is a long-horizon task
sections.lead: One environment can force 30–60+ decisions across systems, people, policies and evolving state.
sections.task: Resolve the escalation, preserve the account, follow policy, and leave every system consistent.
sections.note: The agent must read, decide, message, update records, trigger actions, recover from failures and verify the result.
